references.text: God calls Abram and promises to bless him and make him a great nation – the original promise renewed to Isaac.
God promises Abraham all the land he sees, to him and his descendants forever – a central land promise renewed to Isaac.
God makes a covenant with Abraham and promises his descendants the land from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates.
God's oath-bound promise to Abraham of numerous descendants and blessing – the oath God refers to when confirming the promise to Isaac.
God appears to Isaac again and confirms the promise of presence and blessing with the words 'I am with you'.
God renews the promise of land, descendants, and presence to Jacob, Isaac's son, and carries forward the covenant promises.
God confirms the promise of fruitfulness and land to Jacob, who continues the patriarchal promises.
Paul discusses the promise given to Abraham and his offspring, showing how the covenant promises are fulfilled in Christ.
Jacob's blessing confirms and continues Isaac's experience of living as a stranger while waiting for God's promise of the land.
Direct retelling of God's promise to Jacob that confirms the continuity of the promise given to Isaac in the source verse.
The original covenant (Abraham) and confirmation of the covenant (Isaac) share an identical structure regarding living as strangers and eternal possession.
